source: KICD Environmental Activities, First Published in 2017; Revised 2024 (text layer)
status: outcomes from KICD's text, word for word; skills, prerequisites and misconceptions not yet mapped

learning_experiences: share information on personal and common items found at home,
draw, colour and display personal and common items used at home,
recite poems or sing songs on personal items,
match personal and common items at home with their uses,
observe pictures or animations of different materials used for cleaning personal and common items,
improvise cleaning materials at home or school,
manipulate a digital device to watch video clips or observe a demonstration from a resource person on cleaning personal and common items found at home,
use water sparingly to clean personal items and dry them appropriately,
practise cleaning utensils using suitable soap and soft material,
observe safety and hygiene when handling waste materials to avoid communicable diseases,
sort and dispose of waste appropriately after cleaning personal and common items.
key_inquiry_questions: How can we keep our home clean?
Why should we keep our home environment clean?
sub_strands.core_competences: Critical thinking and Problem-solving: learner enhances innovative thinking in improvising cleaning materials using locally available resources.
sub_strands.values: Responsibility: learner enhances self-drive when cleaning utensils at home.
sub_strands.pcis: Learner observes safety and hygiene when washing hands after handling waste materials to avoid communicable diseases.
sub_strands.links: The skill of sorting draws knowledge learnt in pre-number concepts in Mathematical Activities.

outcomes.text: differentiate between personal and common items used at home
identify materials used for cleaning personal and common items at home
clean personal and common items using locally available materials
advocate for a clean home environment for self and others’ well-being

learning_experiences: talk about family needs and wants,
draw items that represent family wants,
observe pictures and photographs of different places where family needs are met,
draw and colour places where family needs are met,
match places or facilities within the locality where family needs are met,
sort and group pictures of goods and services into family needs and wants,
watch video clips/listen to a resource person on different family needs and wants,
draw and colour items that represent different family needs and wants,
observe pictures of different meals taken at different times of the day,
keep a daily record of meals eaten at home or school for one week,
sort and group different food items into meals and snacks,
play a game of picking out flashcards/paper cuttings/pictures that show family needs and wants.
key_inquiry_questions: How can we meet our family needs?
sub_strands.core_competences: Citizenship: learner develops awareness of the local environment when matching places or facilities within the locality where family needs are met.
sub_strands.values: Love: learner portrays a caring attitude towards peers when playing games of picking out flashcards/paper cuttings/pictures that show family needs and wants.
sub_strands.pcis: Social economic issues: learner enhances financial literacy when sorting and grouping pictures of goods and services into family needs and wants.
sub_strands.links: Family needs and wants relate to the skill of counting, sorting, and grouping in Mathematical Activities.

outcomes.text: mention differences between family needs and wants
identify places within the locality where family needs are met
classify family needs and wants for financial literacy awareness
prioritise family needs over family wants
appreciate family needs and wants within the locality

learning_experiences: use video clips or pictures to find out how to keep the school environment clean,
walk around the school compound to find out dangerous places and items,
draw or write down dangerous places and items in school,
practise cleaning the school environment,
recite poems or sing songs about a clean school environment,
role play ways of giving first aid to common accidents in school (suffocation, falls, burns, cuts, choking),
make papier-mâché art of appropriate objects or models from paper waste.
key_inquiry_questions: How can you keep the school environment clean and safe?
sub_strands.core_competences: Self-efficacy: learner develops the skill of knowing the school by walking around the school compound to find out dangerous places and items.
sub_strands.values: Unity: learner enhances cooperation when cleaning the school environment in groups.
sub_strands.pcis: Social Economic Issues: learner develops disaster risk reduction when role-playing ways of giving first aid to common accidents in school.
sub_strands.links: Paper waste recycling relates to concepts of making papier-mâché in Creative Activities.

outcomes.text: name ways of keeping the school environment clean
identify common accidents at school
clean the school environment for the well-being of self and others
advocate for a clean and safe school environment

learning_experiences: find information on the meaning of colours on the Kenya national flag,
manipulate a digital device to watch videos or observe pictures with colours of the Kenya national flag,
draw and colour the national flag,
role-play the expected behaviour when raising and lowering the Kenya national flag,
listen to audio-visual clips or read print materials to identify occasions when the Kenya national anthem is sung.
key_inquiry_questions: How can you show respect for the Kenya National flag?
sub_strands.core_competences: Citizenship: learner develops active community skills when observing the expected behaviour related to the Kenya national flag and national anthem.
sub_strands.values: Patriotism: learner enhances loyalty to the nation when singing the national anthem.
sub_strands.pcis: Citizenship: learner enhances social cohesion and nationalism when singing the Kenya national anthem.
sub_strands.links: Features of the Kenya national flag relate to learning of colours in Creative Activities.

outcomes.text: identify the meaning of colours on the Kenya national flag
name events in which Kenya’s national anthem is sung
observe etiquette when raising and lowering the Kenya national flag
appreciate the importance of the national anthem

learning_experiences: listen to age-appropriate stories involving expectations and experiences on Child Rights and Responsibilities (parental care, health care, protection from exploitation and cruelty),
listen to a resource person on Child Rights and Responsibilities in a home or school,
use multimedia resources to explore the responsibilities of children at home and in school,
work with peers to role-play responsibilities of children in school,
perform age-appropriate responsibilities at school.
key_inquiry_questions: Why are child rights and responsibilities important at home and school?
sub_strands.core_competences: Communication and Collaboration: learner develops teamwork when role-playing the responsibilities of children in school.
sub_strands.values: Social Justice: learner enhances equity when performing age-appropriate responsibilities at school.
sub_strands.pcis: Citizenship: learner enhances Child Rights awareness when sharing own expectations, experiences, duties and responsibilities at home or school.
sub_strands.links: Listening to a resource person on Child Rights and Responsibilities relates to active listening and speaking in English Language Activities.

outcomes.text: outline Child Rights and Responsibilities at home and in the school
carry out the responsibilities of a child at home and in school
appreciate Child Rights and Responsibilities for the attainment of social justice

learning_experiences: physical features on the way to a local market,
draw and colour physical features found on the way to the local market,
model main physical features found on the way to the local market,
label and match pictures of parts of the road for the safety of self and others (vehicle use and pedestrian walkways),
manipulate digital devices to watch video clips or observe pictures of activities that take place in a market,
listen to a resource person on activities that take place in a market,
visit the nearest market to find out activities that take place,
role play buying and selling activities to recognise the interdependence and connections of people found in a market,
make a shop corner using locally available materials.
key_inquiry_questions: How can you locate your local market?
sub_strands.core_competences: Citizenship: learner recognises the interdependence and connections of people found in a market.
sub_strands.values: Integrity: learner enhances honest and fair negotiations when role-playing buying and selling.
sub_strands.pcis:
Citizenship: learner enhances acknowledgement for self and others when interacting with people found in a market.
Financial Literacy: learner develops spending skills when visiting the nearest market to find out activities that take place.
sub_strands.links: Buying and selling in a market relates to the concept of money in Mathematical Activities.

outcomes.text: identify physical features on the way to a local market
locate local market using physical features
identify activities that take place in a market
value things and people found in a market

learning_experiences: discuss weather conditions at different times of the day,
draw weather symbols to represent different weather conditions and display them in class,
observe and record prevailing weather conditions as an outdoor activity in collaboration with peers,
make a weather record or chart using weather symbols for one week,
play relevant and educative computer games on weather conditions,
observe pictures and video clips to identify ways of responding to various weather conditions,
role play on ways of responding to various weather conditions,
use weather symbols to interpret weather conditions at different times of the day,
participate in a class contest, on narrating the previous week’s weather occurrences from a weather chart.
key_inquiry_questions: Why do we need to predict the weather?
sub_strands.core_competences: Digital Literacy: learner interacts with digital technology when playing relevant and educative games on weather conditions.
sub_strands.values:
Unity: learner develops cooperation when observing and recording prevailing weather conditions as an outdoor activity.
Integrity: learner develops honesty when observing and recording weather conditions for one week.
sub_strands.pcis:
Life Skills: learner develops effective communication skills when participating in a class contest, on narrating weather occurrences from weather chart recordings.
Learner Support Programs: learner develops career guidance skills when creating a weather record using weather symbols for one week.
sub_strands.links: Drawing weather symbols relates to the skill of drawing and colouring in Creative Activities.

outcomes.text: identify weather conditions at different times of the day
create a weather record, using weather symbols
predict weather conditions at different times of the day
develop curiosity in weather conditions experienced in the locality

learning_experiences: walk within the school compound or visit the school neighbourhood to observe types of soil,
model soil ribbons using soil samples,
observe modelled ribbons to find out which soil sample makes smooth long ribbons,
classify types of soil depending on the length of ribbons made and size of particles,
make paper cuttings or pictures of different types of soil and create a portfolio,
model different objects using soil,
clean the working area and wash hands with soap and clean running water after handling soil.
key_inquiry_questions: How can you identify different types of soil in our environment?
sub_strands.core_competences: Learning to Learn: learner develops the skill of learning independently when modelling soil ribbons using soil samples and finding out the soil sample that makes smooth long ribbons.
sub_strands.values: Unity: learner develops cooperation skills when modelling objects with different types of soil.
sub_strands.pcis: Health Promotion issues: learner develops preventive health skills when cleaning the working area and hands with soap and clean running water after handling soil to prevent communicable diseases.
sub_strands.links: Modelling objects using soil draws knowledge from modelling techniques in Creative Activities.

outcomes.text: identify types of soil found in the locality
classify types of soil in the locality
make items from soil
appreciate different types of soil in the immediate environment

learning_experiences: observe pictures and photographs of different sources of light in the environment,
manipulate objects in the presence of light to form shadows,
practise switching off lights when not in use and during day time,
create light conservation messages,
make posters with simple messages on the conservation of light
type messages on the conservation of light using digital devices,
recite poems or sing songs on the conservation of light.
key_inquiry_questions: How can we conserve light in our environment?
Why should we conserve light in our environment?
sub_strands.core_competences: Communication: learner develops writing skills when making posters with simple messages on the conservation of light to create awareness.
sub_strands.values: Unity: learner develops cooperation skills when manipulating objects in the presence of light to form shadows for enjoyment.
sub_strands.pcis: Social Economic Issues: learner develops financial skills when practising switching off lights when not in use and during day time.
sub_strands.links: Posters on energy conservation relate to writing skills in English Language Activities.

outcomes.text: identify sources of light in the environment
manipulate objects in the presence of light to form shadows for enjoyment
describe a variety of ways of conserving light for a sustainable supply of light energy
appreciate different sources of light in the environment

learning_experiences: explore various ways of storing water at home and school,
draw items used to store water at home and school,
practise storing water in bottles and water cans at home and school,
watch video clips, pictures and photographs on appropriate ways of storing water at home and school,
share experiences on why water is stored at home and school,
visit with peers in the neighbourhood to identify different ways of storing water.
key_inquiry_questions: Why do we store water at home and in school?
sub_strands.core_competences: Communication and Collaboration: learner develops teamwork when walking around the neighbourhood to identify different ways of storing water.
sub_strands.values:
Responsibility: learner enhances hard work skills when storing water in bottles and water cans for future use at home and school.
Social Justice: learner enhances cooperation when making visits to the neighbourhood to identify different ways of storing water.
sub_strands.pcis: Health Promotion Issues: learner develops preventive health skills and awareness when storing water appropriately at home and school to prevent communicable diseases.
sub_strands.links: Drawing items used to store water relates to the skill of drawing and colouring in Creative Activities.

outcomes.text: identify ways of storing water at home and school
conserve water at home and school for future use
state the importance of keeping water safe for people and animal use
appreciate safe water storage to prevent health risks to self and others

learning_experiences: observe pictures, photographs or watch video clips of people watering, manuring and mulching plants,
water, manure and mulch for some plants in the school compound,
observe pictures, photographs or video clips of healthy plants that have been conserved,
write plant protection messages by hand or electronic device,
recite poems or sing songs on plant protection.
key_inquiry_questions: How can you care for plants in the environment?
sub_strands.core_competences: Creativity and Imagination: learner develops originality when creating plant protection messages using own handwriting, or electronic resources.
sub_strands.values: Responsibility: learner develops self-drive skills when writing plant protection messages by hand, or electronic resources.
sub_strands.pcis: Citizenship: learner develops environmental education and climate change skills when watering, manuring, and mulching plants in the school compound.
sub_strands.links: Messages on plant protection relate to writing skills in English Language Activities.

outcomes.text: identify ways of caring for plants using locally available materials
perform plant-care activities using locally available materials
advocate for plant protection for environmental sustainability

learning_experiences: observe pictures and photographs of different food items from animals,
observe and name pictures of animals that provide food,
sort and group food items from animals and display them in class,
listen to a resource person on ways of caring for animals,
discuss the importance of fair treatment of animals,
observe videos on ways of keeping an animal shelter clean,
practise feeding and cleaning animal shelter (for small domestic animal) at home or school,
wash hands with soap and water after cleaning the animal shelter,
dispose of waste appropriately after cleaning an animal shelter while observing safety.
key_inquiry_questions: Why should an animal stay in a clean place?
sub_strands.core_competences: Communication and Collaboration: learner develops speaking and listening skills when discussing the importance of fair treatment of animals in groups.
sub_strands.values: Love: learner develops empathy skills when feeding and cleaning animal shelters at home or school.
sub_strands.pcis: Social Economic Issues: learner develops animal welfare awareness when participating in cleaning animal shelters at home or school.
sub_strands.links: Matching, sorting, and grouping food items from animals draws the skills of sorting and grouping in Mathematical Activities.

outcomes.text: identify food items from animals
relate food items with respective animals
carry out activities of caring for animals in the locality
advocate for clean and secure animal shelters to reduce risks to the animals

indicators.indicator: Ability to practise proper hygiene at home and school. Ability to practise good healthy habits at home and school. Ability to practise proper sanitation at home and school. Ability to observe etiquette when raising and lowering the Kenya national flag. Ability to carry out duties and responsibilities as a child. Ability to observe safety precautions in the immediate environment.

levels.EE: Practises proper hygiene at home and school most frequently. Practises good healthy habits at home and school most frequently. Practises proper sanitation at home and school most frequently. Observes etiquette when raising and lowering the Kenya national flag very keenly. Carries out duties and responsibilities as a child very keenly. Observes safety precautions in the immediate environment most keenly.
levels.ME: Practises proper hygiene at home and school. Practises good healthy habits at home and school. Practises proper sanitation at home and school. Observes etiquette when raising and lowering the Kenya national flag keenly. Carries out duties and responsibilities as a child keenly. Observes safety precautions in the immediate environment keenly.
levels.AE: Practises proper hygiene at home and school occasionally. Practises good healthy habits at home and school occasionally. Practises proper sanitation at home and school occasionally. Observes etiquette when raising and lowering the Kenya national flag less keenly. Carries out duties and responsibilities as a child less keenly. Observes safety precautions in the immediate environment less keenly.
levels.BE: Rarely practises proper hygiene at home and school. Rarely practises good healthy habits at home and school. Rarely practises proper sanitation at home and school. Observes etiquette when raising and lowering the Kenya national flag with prompts. Carries out duties and responsibilities as a child with prompts. Observes safety precautions in the immediate environment with prompts.

indicators.indicator: Ability to predict weather conditions at different times of the day.

levels.EE: Predicts weather conditions at different times of the day most precisely.
levels.ME: Predicts weather conditions at different times of the day.
levels.AE: Predicts weather conditions at different times of the day less precisely.
levels.BE: Predicts weather conditions at different times of the day with prompts.

indicators.indicator: Ability to classify types of soil in the locality.

levels.EE: Classifies types of soil in the locality most precisely.
levels.ME: Classifies types of soil in the locality precisely.
levels.AE: Classifies types of soil in the locality less precisely.
levels.BE: Classifies types of soil in the locality with prompts.

indicators.indicator: Ability to describe a variety of ways of conserving light.

levels.EE: Extensively describes a variety of ways of conserving light from various sources.
levels.ME: Describes a variety of ways of conserving light.
levels.AE: Describes a few ways of conserving light.
levels.BE: Describes a few ways of conserving light when given hints.

indicators.indicator: Ability to describe the conservation of water for people and animal use. Ability to conserve water for people and animal use. Ability to carry out activities for caring for plants using locally available materials. Ability to identify animals as sources of food that people eat . Ability to carry out activities of caring for animals in the locality. Suggested Learning Resources, Assessment Methods, and Non-Formal Activities Suggested learning resources ● Approved curriculum support materials ● Resources from the local environment (home and school) ● Flashcards ● Pictures, newspapers, magazines, journals ● Digital devices ● Assorted farm equipment ● Assorted cleaning agents, tools, and equipment ● Resource persons Non-formal Activities that Support Learning ● School routine activities such as cleaning, flag raising, worship activities ● Games and sports ● Clubs and societies

levels.EE: Describes varied conservation methods of water for people and animal use with in-depth details. Very often conserves water for people and animal use using appropriate varied methods. Carries out watering, manuring, and mulching plants using locally available materials consistently. Identifies animals as sources of food that people eat with a lot of details. Most frequently carries out activities of caring for animals in the locality.
levels.ME: Describes conservation methods of water for human and animal use. Conserves water for people and animal use. Carries out watering, manuring, and mulching plants using locally available materials. Identifies animals as sources of food that people eat. Carries out activities of caring for animals in the locality. Suggested assessment methods ● Observation ● Written test ● Oral questions ● Aural questions ● Peer assessment ● Self-assessment
levels.AE: Describes conservation methods of water for people and animal use with minimal details. Occasionally conserves water for people and animal use. Carries out watering, manuring, or mulching plants using locally available materials inconsistently. Identifies animals as sources of food that people eat with minimal details. Occasionally carries out activities of caring for animals in the locality.
levels.BE: Describes conservation methods of water for people and animal use without details. Rarely conserves water for people and animal use with prompts. Carries out watering/manuring/mulc hing plants using locally available materials with prompts. Identifies animals as sources of food that people eat without details. Rarely carries out activities of caring for animals in the locality.
